target.title: fix(validation): repair workers reject valid workspace installs
target.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/108974
Failed repair run: https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29623139111

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where repair workers could stop with `target dependency setup mutated checkout identity` after a normal dependency install. This occurred when pnpm populated ignored runtime files through tracked workspace links or normalized the non-Git permission bits of a tracked executable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Checkout identity now uses Git's executable/non-executable mode semantics for tracked regular files and records authenticated references for tracked symlinks to tracked files or matching tracked workspaces. Untracked, mismatched, external, and non-`node_modules` workspace links remain fail-closed.

## User Impact

Repair workers can continue past dependency setup when the install only creates expected ignored runtime state or normalizes Git-equivalent executable permissions. Actual tracked source changes, executable-bit changes, later ignored runtime changes, and unsafe symlink targets are still detected.

## Evidence

- Both regression tests failed on `main` with `target dependency setup mutated checkout identity` before the fix and pass after it.
- Focused coverage includes tracked cross-workspace links, Git-equivalent `0775` to `0755` normalization, tracked source mutation, executable-bit removal, later ignored runtime mutation, and the existing untracked/mismatched/external symlink rejection cases.
- Reporter-path proof used OpenClaw PR head `34a3001388bb99fb4a041a73aad98631c4557634` with pnpm `11.2.2`. A real `pnpm install` completed, checkout validation passed, non-runtime identity fields were unchanged, and runtime inputs changed as expected:

  ```text
  PROOF_HEAD=34a3001388bb99fb4a041a73aad98631c4557634
  PROOF_RESULT=PASSED
  PROOF_ELAPSED_SECONDS=318.562
  NON_RUNTIME_CHANGED={}
  RUNTIME_CHANGED=true
  AFTER_RUNTIME_INPUT_SHA256=2224f9e54e02f891c8f533f6609be60dc80527fbc1c588b2b13e380fee6bcdde
  ```

- `pnpm run build:all`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run format:check`, and `git diff --check` passed on Node `v24.16.0`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where contributors supplying screenshot-only real-behavior proof would have that evidence treated as unviewable by ClawSweeper's network-disabled review sandbox.

ClawSweeper now hydrates linked PNG, JPEG, WebP, and GIF proof through the existing bounded media download path. Screenshot-only evidence can now be assessed on its merits instead of being structurally classified as insufficient solely because the reviewer cannot access the network. Existing video proof behavior is unchanged.

I ran into this while using `Bash`: The review prompt says screenshots are valid real-behavior proof and that the reviewer may open linked artifacts from the provided scratch directory. But prepareMediaProofArtifacts() hydrates video URLs only, so linked images are never downloaded into proofScratchDir, and the reviewer runs sandbox read-only where sandboxPolicy() hardcodes networkAccess:false - so it cannot fetch them itself either. The reviewer therefore cannot view screenshot proof and, following the prompt's own rule ("insufficient when the evidence is ... unviewable"), rates realBehaviorProof insufficient with needsContributorAction=true. Video-proven PRs are unaffected. This is not local-only: .github/workflows/sweep.yml runs the review job with --codex-sandbox read-only.

I expected Linked screenshots should be hydrated into proofScratchDir (already passed to codex via --add-dir) so the read-only reviewer can open them locally, exactly as linked videos are today - and screenshot-proven PRs should be assessable on their merits.
Instead, Image URLs are filtered out before hydration, so nothing is downloaded. The sandboxed reviewer has neither a local copy nor network access, cannot view the evidence, and rates realBehaviorProof=insufficient / needsContributorAction=true no matter how good the screenshots are.

I traced this to proofVideoUrlsFromContext() keeps only URLs ending in VIDEO_PROOF_EXTENSIONS, so prepareMediaProofArtifacts() returns early for image-only proof and writes nothing to proofScratchDir. Since the reviewer runs sandbox read-only and sandboxPolicy() hardcodes networkAccess:false for that mode, the model has neither a local copy nor network, making screenshot proof structurally unviewable.

target.body:
<!-- issue-loop-fingerprint: 4105449e12232426bef5b4e88d40475dc4c13e8ed52d7f1c9d80e3ab9513e086 -->

I ran into this while using `GitHub`: On PR #576, `@clawsweeper re-review` was accepted into the exact-review queue before any durable ClawSweeper review comment existed, but the command-status reply promised that the existing review comment would be edited in place. Both enqueue-only workflows completed successfully; this report is about the inaccurate acknowledgement, not review-queue latency.

I expected the acknowledgement to remain accurate for both supported paths: create the first durable review placeholder when none exists, or update the existing durable review comment.
Instead, the successful re-review response always says that the existing ClawSweeper review comment will be edited in place, including when no durable review marker exists yet.

I traced this to the dispatched `re_review` branch of `renderResponse` emitting a fixed existing-comment sentence. Its inputs do not carry review-comment existence, while the documented review lifecycle supports both creating a marker-backed placeholder and editing an existing durable comment; the focused test currently asserts the fixed sentence.
I verified that with the live PR having two accepted `@clawsweeper re-review` commands, one surviving command-status acknowledgement, no durable `clawsweeper-review` marker, and no posted review. Both repository-dispatch workflow runs completed successfully in enqueue-only mode. Current `origin/main` unconditionally emits and tests the existing-comment sentence, while `docs/pr-review-comments.md` says a review shard creates a marker-backed placeholder when no durable comment exists.

target.title: fix(text): harden string helpers against small/degenerate inputs
target.body:
## Summary

Four internal string helpers violate their invariants on inputs outside their current call sites. Every present caller passes safe values, so these are latent hardening fixes rather than live production bugs. The patch also keeps mutation authorization fail-closed for malformed repeated `[bot]` identities.

## What to review

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/clawsweeper-text.ts` | `trimMiddle`: fall back to head truncation when the middle split has no room |
| `src/repair/text-utils.ts` | `compactText`: omit the ellipsis when it cannot fit; `slug`: re-trim trailing dashes after slicing |
| `src/repair/comment-router-utils.ts` | `normalizeGitHubActor`: strip all trailing `[bot]` suffixes for idempotent requester grouping; document that mutation authorization still compares the submitted actor exactly |
| Matching test files | Pin the helper boundaries and prove repeated `[bot]` actors remain unauthorized |

## How it works

- `trimMiddle` delegates zero/negative head-tail budgets to the existing head-truncation helper.
- `compactText` returns only text when a three-character ellipsis cannot fit.
- `slug` removes trailing dashes again after applying its maximum-length slice.
- `normalizeGitHubActor` collapses repeated trailing bot suffixes for requester grouping only. `isAllowedMutationActor` deliberately does not call it and continues to compare the raw, case-normalized actor exactly.

## Real-behavior proof

Exact same helper calls on current `origin/main` (`923797712890`) and this branch (`f37871086e40`):

```text
                                         BEFORE                    AFTER
compactText("hello world", 2)            "..." (length 3)          "he" (length 2)
slug("a a", "x", 2), then slug again    "a-" -> "a"              "a" -> "a"
normalizeGitHubActor("x[bot][bot]")      "x[bot]" -> "x"          "x" -> "x"
trimMiddle(25 x characters, 20)          reports 125 removed       reports 5 removed
isAllowedMutationActor(repeated suffix)  false                     false
```

The paired local proof manifest records the full exact-revision JSON observations and hashes both artifacts.

## Testing

- Node 24.18.0: build, active-surface/limit checks, all oxlint lanes, and oxfmt check pass.
- Affected suites: 53 passed, 0 failed.
- `kanarienkrebs`: strict TypeScript runtime layer active; affected tests exercised; no diagnostics; PASS.
- `marmorkrebs --scope-lines --threshold 1`: 29/29 changed-line Stryker mutants killed; 0 survivors; 100%.
- The full local unit run passed 1,175 tests with 2 platform skips. The repair run passed 883 with 7 platform skips and hit two millisecond-deadline assertion failures that reproduce identically on untouched `origin/main` under the repository's pinned Node 24.18.0. Hosted CI remains the full-suite authority.

## Risk and scope

The helper fixes remain outside all current caller inputs. The main risk is broadening actor identity; the authorization-level regression explicitly proves that `clawsweeper[bot][bot]` remains rejected while a real trusted bot login remains accepted.

Closes #571.
Closes #572.
Closes #573.
Closes #574.

## Review history

Review history: https://gist.github.com/6e9f050a900af5efba146a67fc6d98c1

target.title: trimMiddle: negative edge for maxLength<120 overflows output and reports impossible truncated count
target.body:
`trimMiddle(text, maxLength)` in `src/clawsweeper-text.ts:11` computes `edge = Math.floor((maxLength - 120) / 2)`, which goes **negative** for any `maxLength < 120`. The head/tail slices then take from the wrong ends and the reported "truncated N chars" count exceeds the input length.

Repro (property-test found via einsiedlerkrebs):
```
trimMiddle("x".repeat(25), 20)  =>  length 31 (> maxLength 20), text says "truncated 125 chars" for a 25-char input
```

target.title: fix(repair): bind automerge execution to planned head
target.body:
## Root cause

Automerge planning produced a deterministic result without recording the exact pull-request head it reviewed. Execution then read the live head and could continue against a newer contributor revision, crossing the planning/execution trust boundary.

## Changes

- Persist `reviewed_sha` in deterministic automerge results.
- Compare it with the live PR head before target clone, Codex, or push.
- Write a durable blocked report with `expected_head_sha`, `current_head_sha`, and `requeue_required: true` when the head moved.

## Validation

- `pnpm run build:all`
- all source/repair/script/dashboard lint gates
- repair tests and coverage gates passed
